sentences.text:
Petitione
 Through: Mr. Rachit Gupta, Advocate with
 petitioners.

versus
 The State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr. .....
Resp  Through: Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, APP for  the State with SI Sita Ram, P.S  Karawal Nagar.

Respondent no. 2 in person.
 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE SWARANA KANTA SHARMA
ORDER % 18.04.2023 CRL.M.A. 10075/2023 (early hearing)
1. By way of present application filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C), the applicant seeks early hearing of the petition.
2. Heard.
In view of the reasons stated, the application is allowed.
Let the petition be taken up today.
3. The next date of hearing i.e. 15.05.2023 stands cancelled.

4. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) has been filed by petitioners praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 526/2019, registered at Police Station Karawal Nagar, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
5. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

6. All the petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr.
Rachit Gupta and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Sita Ram from Police Station Karawal Nagar, Delhi.

7. Brief facts of the present case are that on the basis of a complaint lodged by respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 526/2019, Police Station Karawal Nagar, Delhi, for the offences punishable under Virender Pal Singh & Ors vs The State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193315867/
1 Section 498A/406/34 of IPC was registered against petitioners.

sentences.text:
It is stated that during the pendency of the case, the parties have mutually decided to settle the instant matter before Counselling Cell,
Family Courts, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi, on 18.05.2022.
8.

entities.text:
Counselling Cell,
Family Courts, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before Counselling Cell, Family Courts, Karkardooma Courts,
Delhi on 18.05.2022.
9.

entities.text:
Counselling Cell, Family Courts, Karkardooma Courts,
Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.

10. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- in three installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 2,00,000/- paid to respondent no.2 at the time recording of statement of first motion;
b. Second installment of Rs. 2,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statement of second motion; c. Third/Final instalment of Rs. 1,00,000/-
to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

11. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 1,00,000/- today, i.e., 18.04.2023 vide DD No. 208469 drawn on Bank of Baroda,
Chattarpur, New Delhi, and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

12. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

13. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 526/2019, registered at Police Station Karawal Nagar, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
14.
The present petition stands disposed of.
15. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J APRIL 18, 2023/
